best_idea: Cap the client frame rate with a single schedule anchor that advances by a fixed period and re-anchors when the setting changes, and give each loading frame a fixed millisecond slice of asset work.
decision_why: Keep the player and device fps cap and the time-sliced loading, replace the thread sleep with a requestAnimationFrame gate and add the overrun clamp the donor lacks; a fixed cap also saves battery and heat on a phone.
acceptance: A Vitest on the pacer: at a 30 fps target, 10 s of simulated frames gives 300 ± 3 frame starts; after a 200 ms stall, at most one frame runs back to back and the frame after it waits up to one period (33 ms).
